text:
The text contrasts two opposing views on human nature. William Golding’s Lord of the Flies presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, illustrated by boys descending into savagery when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy suggests that society is the corrupting force, implying that humanity’s natural state is one of goodness and freedom. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the origin of human behavior and morality, but they differ fundamentally in their conclusions: Golding argues for innate evil, while Rousseau argues for innate goodness corrupted by external structures.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
